terms.definition: The amount of energy per unit mass or volume of a fuel or resource.
terms.examiner: Fossil fuels and uranium are high; most renewables are low, so need large areas.

terms.definition: The way the output of some energy resources varies with conditions that cannot be controlled, such as wind speed and sunlight.
terms.examiner: Leads to the need for storage or back-up supplies.

terms.definition: The actual output of a power station or device as a proportion of its maximum possible output over a period.
terms.examiner: Low for wind and solar because they do not run at full power all the time.

terms.definition: Storing surplus energy when demand is low and using it to meet peaks in demand.
terms.examiner: Pumped-storage hydroelectric power is the usual example.

terms.definition: Removing carbon dioxide from power station emissions and storing it underground.
terms.examiner: Evaluate it: it uses energy and storage sites are limited.

terms.definition: Injecting water, sand and chemicals at high pressure to crack shale and release gas or oil.
terms.examiner: Know the concerns: groundwater contamination, water use and induced earthquakes.

terms.definition: Splitting the nucleus of a heavy atom such as uranium-235 by neutron bombardment, releasing energy and more neutrons.
terms.examiner: Fusion joins light nuclei and is not yet a commercial energy source.

terms.definition: The ratio of the energy obtained from a resource to the energy used to obtain it.
terms.examiner: A resource with a ratio near 1 is not worth exploiting.
